item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Baobab Platform Mentorship Application offers African young people an opportunity to connect with experienced role models and receive career-focused mentorship tailored to their goals, interests, aspirations, and professional development needs. Designed for young Africans between the ages of 18 and 30, the Baobab Mentorship Program uses a gender-matching approach to connect participants with suitable mentors from the private and/or public sectors. The program is intended to help participants develop meaningful professional relationships and gain guidance as they navigate their career journeys. Applications for the 2026 cohort are open, and eligible applicants are encouraged to complete the required mentorship course and submit their certificate before applying.

2026 Baobab Platform Mentorship Program

The Baobab Platform Mentorship Program is designed around the idea that access to the right mentor can help young people make better-informed decisions about their education, career development, professional aspirations, and future opportunities.

Through the program, participants are matched with role-model mentors according to factors such as:

  • Career goals
  • Common interests
  • Professional aspirations
  • Personal development objectives
  • Gender-matching considerations

Mentors may come from either the private sector or public sector, depending on the individual participant’s profile and the type of guidance that would be most relevant to their goals.

Rather than providing a one-size-fits-all mentoring experience, the program seeks to create connections that are relevant to each participant’s ambitions.

Who Is the Baobab Mentorship Program For?

The program is specifically designed for African youth aged 18 to 30.

Applicants who fall within this age range and are interested in receiving mentorship related to their career development can consider applying, provided they meet the program’s additional requirements.

The opportunity can be particularly relevant to young Africans who are:

  • Exploring potential career paths
  • Seeking professional guidance and role models
  • Developing their career goals and aspirations
  • Interested in connecting with experienced professionals
  • Looking for mentorship from leaders in the public or private sector
  • Seeking to expand their professional perspective and networks

Mandatory Baobab Mentorship Course

One of the most important requirements for applicants is the completion of the Baobab Mentorship course.

Applicants cannot simply submit the mentorship application without completing this prerequisite. To be eligible for the cohort, applicants must:

  1. Complete Baobab’s Mentorship course.
  2. Obtain the course certificate.
  3. Submit the certificate together with the mentorship application form.

This requirement means prospective applicants should begin the process early rather than waiting until immediately before the application deadline.

Access the Baobab Mentorship Course

Applicants can access the required mentorship course through the following link:

Access the Baobab Mentorship Course

A Baobab account is required to access the course. Applicants who do not already have an account should therefore take this into consideration when planning their application.

Access the Baobab Platform

The Baobab Platform is the platform through which applicants can access the relevant program resources and course.

Access Baobab Platform

Applicants should ensure that they have access to their account and are able to complete the required course before proceeding with the mentorship application.

How the Mentorship Matching Works

A distinctive feature of this program is its approach to matching participants with mentors.

The program is designed to gender-match participants with role-model mentors while also taking into consideration the participant’s career goals, interests, and aspirations.

This approach is intended to help create mentorship relationships that are more closely aligned with the participant’s individual circumstances and professional direction.

Depending on the applicant’s goals, the mentor may have experience in the private sector, public sector, or another relevant professional environment.

The matching process therefore aims to connect young people with individuals who can provide relevant perspectives and guidance based on their aspirations.

Why Mentorship Can Be Valuable for Young Professionals

For young people beginning or developing their professional journeys, having access to an experienced mentor can provide perspectives that may not be available through formal education alone.

A mentorship relationship can potentially help participants:

  • Gain insights into professional environments and career pathways.
  • Better understand their career interests and aspirations.
  • Learn from someone with practical professional experience.
  • Receive guidance when making career-related decisions.
  • Develop greater awareness of professional expectations.
  • Build meaningful relationships with experienced role models.
  • Gain perspectives on navigating professional challenges.
  • Strengthen their understanding of opportunities within their areas of interest.

The value of the experience will ultimately depend on the participant’s engagement, preparation, communication, and willingness to learn from the mentor.

Application Requirements

Applicants should pay close attention to the requirements before submitting their forms.

The key requirement explicitly stated for this cohort is completion of the Baobab Mentorship course and submission of the resulting certificate with the application.

Applicants should therefore have the following ready:

  • A Baobab account to access the mentorship course.
  • Completion of the required Baobab Mentorship course.
  • The certificate obtained after completing the course.
  • Accurate information for the mentorship application form.
  • Honest responses to all questions in the application.

Completing the course as early as possible is advisable because applicants need to obtain the certificate before submitting their mentorship application.

Importance of Providing Accurate Information

The mentorship application has been designed to provide applicants with fair and equal consideration.

Applicants are therefore expected to complete the application form carefully and provide information that accurately represents their circumstances, experiences, interests, goals, and aspirations.

The organizers state that information submitted through the application will be treated as confidential and used to facilitate the Baobab Platform Mentorship Program in partnership with Global Give Back Circle.

Applicants should consequently take time to review their answers before submitting the form.

Honesty and Applicant Responsibilities

Applicants are expected to provide honest information throughout the application process.

By completing the application form, applicants pledge that the information they provide is truthful.

Applicants should not misrepresent their qualifications, experiences, circumstances, or any other information requested on the form.

According to the program information, if information submitted by an applicant is found to be dishonest, the program reserves the right to reject the application. In cases where an applicant has already been selected, further action may include dismissal from the program.

For this reason, applicants should ensure that every response is accurate and can be supported if clarification is required.

Apply HERE

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the 2026 Baobab Platform Mentorship Program is 6 September 2026.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to complete the process. Because completion of the required mentorship course and submission of the course certificate are prerequisites, prospective participants should allow sufficient time to:

  1. Create or access their Baobab account.
  2. Complete the required mentorship course.
  3. Obtain the course certificate.
  4. Prepare the necessary application information.
  5. Upload or submit the certificate as required.
  6. Review the completed application.
  7. Submit the application before the deadline.

Late preparation could create unnecessary difficulties, particularly if an applicant has not yet completed the required course.

Learn more HERE

How to Apply for the 2026 Baobab Mentorship Program

Interested applicants can follow these steps:

Step 1: Access the Baobab Platform

Visit the Baobab Platform and make sure you have an active account.

Visit the Baobab Platform

Step 2: Complete the Mentorship Course

Access and complete the required Baobab Mentorship course.

Complete the Mentorship Course

Step 3: Obtain Your Certificate

After completing the course, make sure you obtain the required course certificate.

Step 4: Prepare Your Application

Complete the mentorship application form carefully. Provide accurate information about your background, career goals, interests, aspirations, and other requested information.

Step 5: Submit the Certificate

Ensure that the mentorship course certificate is submitted together with your application, as required for eligibility.

Step 6: Review and Submit

Before submitting, review all information carefully to ensure that your responses are accurate and honest.

The application must be submitted by 6 September 2026.

Important Advice for Applicants

Prospective applicants should not treat the mentorship course as an optional extra. It is specifically identified as an eligibility requirement for the cohort.

It is also advisable to think carefully about your career objectives before completing the application. Since the program considers career goals, common interests, and aspirations when matching participants with mentors, applicants should clearly communicate the areas in which they hope to receive mentorship.

A strong application should therefore be:

  • Accurate
  • Honest
  • Complete
  • Clear about career goals
  • Thoughtful about professional aspirations
  • Submitted with the required mentorship course certificate

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Program 2026 Baobab Platform Mentorship Program
Target participants African youth
Age requirement 18–30 years
Mentorship approach Gender-matched role-model mentors
Mentor sectors Private and/or public sector
Matching considerations Career goals, common interests and aspirations
Mandatory requirement Completion of Baobab Mentorship course
Certificate Must be submitted with the application
Baobab account Required to access the course
Application deadline 6 September 2026
Program partner Global Give Back Circle

Final Thoughts

The 2026 Baobab Platform Mentorship Program provides an opportunity for young Africans aged 18 to 30 to connect with role-model mentors whose professional experience and interests may align with their career goals and aspirations.

The program’s gender-matching approach and consideration of participants’ career objectives, interests, and aspirations are intended to create more relevant mentorship connections. Participants may be matched with mentors from the public and/or private sector, giving them the opportunity to gain perspectives from experienced professionals.

However, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the program’s mandatory prerequisite: completion of the Baobab Mentorship course and submission of the course certificate with the application. Applicants should also ensure that all information provided is accurate and honest.

With the application deadline set for 6 September 2026, eligible African youth should begin the process early, complete the required course, obtain their certificate, and submit a carefully prepared application before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Vechta in Germany is inviting applications for up to three PhD scholarships within the doctoral college “Justice Dimensions of Sustainability-Oriented Transformation Processes in Rural Areas” (PK 060).

Funded by the Hans Böckler Foundation, the doctoral college focuses on understanding the social justice challenges associated with sustainability-oriented transformation processes, with particular attention to rural areas.

The programme brings together research on sustainability, social justice, rural development, environmental change, technological transformation and other related areas. It welcomes researchers from several academic disciplines and supports both qualitative and quantitative research approaches, with quantitative and mixed-methods research explicitly encouraged.

The scholarships are expected to begin between June and September 2027 and can be awarded for a maximum of three years.

The application deadline is November 2, 2026.

About the Doctoral College

The doctoral college is affiliated with the Vechta Institute of Sustainability Transformation in Rural Areas (VISTRA) at the University of Vechta.

Sustainability transformation has become an important subject of scientific, political and social discussion. However, major transformation processes can have different consequences for different groups within society.

While some people may benefit from new technologies, policies and economic opportunities, others may experience negative consequences or what the programme describes as “transformation pains.”

These differences raise important questions about social justice.

The doctoral college seeks to address these questions by investigating how sustainability-oriented transformations affect people and communities and how transformation processes can be designed in ways that are considered fair and socially just.

Particular attention is given to rural areas, where sustainability transformations can have distinctive economic, social, environmental and technological consequences.

The programme aims to make a significant contribution to research in this area through a comparative case study approach across individual doctoral projects.

Research Areas and Possible PhD Topics

The doctoral college provides several examples of research topics that could be explored through doctoral projects. These examples are not intended to represent an exhaustive list.

Transformation of the Energy Sector

Research could examine issues surrounding energy affordability and the emergence of new forms of inequality between urban and rural areas.

Potential areas of investigation include the distribution of costs and benefits associated with energy transitions and how changes in the energy sector affect different communities.

Spatial Justice

Applicants may explore questions related to fairness and equality across geographical spaces.

Possible topics include:

  • Equitable livelihoods
  • Social places
  • Local resilience
  • Rural and urban inequalities
  • Access to opportunities and resources

Normative Uncertainty

Another possible area of research concerns uncertainty about what constitutes the appropriate ethical standard for designing just sustainability transformations.

This could involve examining the theoretical and practical difficulties involved in determining what a fair transformation should look like.

Risk, Uncertainty and Perceived Justice

Research may also examine how risk and uncertainty influence people’s perceptions of justice and injustice during transformation processes.

Socio-Technical Transitions and Innovation

The doctoral college is interested in justice-related questions arising from technological and innovation processes.

Potential examples include:

  • Digitalisation
  • Bio-economy
  • Socio-technical transitions
  • Innovation processes
  • Technological change in rural areas

Nature and Climate Protection Policies

Applicants may investigate the justice-related consequences of policies designed to protect nature and address climate change.

Research could consider issues such as:

  • Urban-rural relationships
  • Climate protection policies
  • Nature conservation
  • Relationships between the Global North and Global South

Gender Justice

Another potential area is the role of gender justice in the design and implementation of sustainability-oriented transformation processes.

Trade Unions and Just Transformations

Applicants may also investigate how trade unions contribute to shaping sustainability transformations and ensuring that these processes are socially just.

The programme is open to other research topics where the proposed project clearly contributes to its overall focus on justice, sustainability transformation and rural areas.

Academic Disciplines

The doctoral college welcomes applications from academic fields that are relevant to its research programme.

These include:

  • Human geography
  • Social sciences
  • Applied ethics
  • Economics
  • Sustainability science
  • Psychology

Research proposals from related academic fields may also be considered where they fit the overall objectives of the doctoral college.

APPLY HERE

Research Methodologies

The programme supports a range of research methodologies.

Both qualitative and quantitative research approaches are welcome.

Applicants proposing quantitative or mixed-methods research are explicitly encouraged to apply.

The comparative case study approach used by the doctoral college provides an opportunity for individual doctoral projects to contribute to a broader understanding of sustainability-oriented transformation processes.

Language Requirements

Applicants are required to have good knowledge of both German and English.

The minimum language levels specified in the call are:

  • German: B2
  • English: C1

Although German language proficiency is required for the application, the doctoral thesis may be written in English.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they can meet the required language standards before submitting their application.

Financial Support

Successful scholarship holders will receive a monthly stipend of €1,650.

The monthly funding consists of:

  • €1,550 basic stipend
  • €100 lump sum for research costs

Additional financial support may also be available.

This includes:

  • A health insurance contribution of up to €100
  • A family allowance, where applicable

The scholarships are awarded for a maximum of three years.

The standard funding period may be extended in justified cases.

Start Date and Duration

The doctoral fellowships are expected to begin between June and September 2027.

Funding can continue for a maximum of three years, subject to the applicable scholarship conditions.

The funding period is intended to provide doctoral researchers with sufficient time to develop and complete their research within the framework of the doctoral college.

Academic and Professional Development

The doctoral college offers more than financial support.

Scholarship holders will participate in an academic environment designed to encourage research development, collaboration and knowledge exchange.

The programme provides:

Thematic Workshops

Scholarship holders will have access to workshops related to the central themes of sustainability transformation and social justice.

Methodological Workshops

Researchers will also have opportunities to strengthen their methodological knowledge and research skills.

Collaborative Research Environment

The doctoral college supports collaboration among scholarship holders and participating researchers.

This is intended to create a motivating and supportive environment where researchers can exchange ideas, discuss challenges and strengthen their individual doctoral projects.

National and International Research Network

The doctoral college has established connections with national and international research institutions.

The network includes:

  • Leuphana University Lüneburg
  • Leibniz Center for Agricultural Landscape Research
  • Basque Center for Climate Change
  • Lund University
  • Copernicus Institute/Utrecht University
  • University of Vermont

These partnerships provide an opportunity to complement and deepen the expertise available within the doctoral college.

They may also provide opportunities for academic exchange and engagement with researchers working on sustainability transformation, climate change, rural development and related issues.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to submit the necessary application documents together with an exposé of no more than 10 pages.

The exposé should clearly outline the proposed doctoral research project and explain how it fits within the research programme of the doctoral college.

The proposal should make clear:

  1. The research problem being addressed
  2. The main research questions
  3. The academic field in which the research is situated
  4. The methodology that will be used
  5. The sustainability transformation being examined
  6. The justice dimensions of the research
  7. The relevance of rural areas to the project
  8. How the project contributes to the broader objectives of the doctoral college

Applicants should ensure that their research proposal is clearly connected to the central theme of justice dimensions of sustainability-oriented transformation processes in rural areas.

Discuss Your Research Project Before Applying

Prospective applicants are encouraged to contact the academic leadership of the doctoral college before submitting their application.

The programme indicates that promising applicants may receive support from the academic leadership in revising and adapting their exposé where necessary.

This support can help ensure that the proposed project fits the themes and requirements of the doctoral programme.

Applicants can contact:

Prof. Dr. Jana Zscheischler
Email: jana.zscheischler@uni-vechta.de

Prof. Dr. John Oliver Engler
Email: john-oliver.engler@uni-vechta.de

The exposé will subsequently undergo academic review.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Up to 3 PhD Scholarships in Germany with €1,650 Monthly Stipend at the University of Vechta

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted exclusively through the Hans Böckler Foundation’s online application portal.

Applicants should prepare the required documents and research exposé before submitting their application.

The application deadline is:

November 2, 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and allow enough time to prepare a well-developed research proposal.

For information about the doctoral college and its research programme, applicants can consult the University of Vechta’s VISTRA doctoral college information.

Selection Process

Doctoral fellowship decisions will be made according to BMBF guidelines and Hans Böckler Foundation selection criteria.

The application process includes academic assessment of the proposed research project.

Promising applicants may be supported in revising their exposé to better align the project with the doctoral college’s research programme and requirements.

The successful scholarship recipients are expected to be announced in May 2027.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should pay close attention to how their proposed research connects with the central focus of the doctoral college.

A strong research proposal should clearly demonstrate:

  • Why the selected sustainability transformation is important
  • Which communities or groups are affected
  • What justice-related questions arise
  • Why rural areas are important to the research
  • What gap in existing research the project will address
  • Which research methodology will be used
  • Why the selected methodology is appropriate
  • How the project contributes to discussions on sustainability and social justice

Applicants proposing quantitative or mixed-methods projects should clearly explain how their methodological approach will help answer their research questions.

It is also advisable to contact the programme leadership before submitting the application, as the doctoral college specifically encourages prospective applicants to discuss their projects in advance.

Conclusion

The University of Vechta’s doctoral college “Justice Dimensions of Sustainability-Oriented Transformation Processes in Rural Areas” provides an opportunity for doctoral researchers to investigate some of the most important questions surrounding sustainability, social justice and rural transformation.

Up to three PhD scholarships will be awarded, with successful researchers receiving a €1,650 monthly stipend, possible additional support for health insurance and family costs, and access to thematic and methodological workshops.

The programme also offers an academic network involving national and international research institutions, providing opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange.

Researchers working in areas such as economics, sustainability science, social sciences, human geography, applied ethics and psychology may find the programme particularly relevant, especially those developing quantitative or mixed-methods research projects.

Prospective applicants should carefully develop an exposé of no more than 10 pages and clearly demonstrate how their research fits within the doctoral college’s focus.

The application deadline is November 2, 2026. Fellowships are expected to begin between June and September 2027 and may run for up to three years.
